description: Add reusable crash-handling to outram-park-digital-twin-engine::app_scaffold: (1) ThreadHealth/CrashReport shared flag; (2) spawn_monitored + spawn_physics_thread_monitored wrap the thread body in catch_unwind and record the panic message; (3) show_crash_modal_if_crashed egui::Modal helper telling the user to restart; (4) SharedState made lock-poison-safe so the GUI reader does not cascade-panic. Wire htgr_sim_v1 (scaffold) and fhr_sim_v2 (engine, raw Arc<Mutex>). tampines fhr_sim_v2 copy NOT mirrored: tampines crate does not depend on the engine crate (would need a new dev-dep + risks a dep cycle) — tracked as follow-up.
title: app_scaffold: thread-panic crash detection + restart notification modal for sims

description: The thermal pincell (op-6tz.12) is LIVE at k_inf=1.39802+/-0.00652 but only verified (physical band), not validated. Run HIGH-tier (net-fetch from_endf) U235/238/O16 + real OpenMC pincell with same materials/geometry and compare k_inf. See REVIEW_MANIFEST op-6tz-thermal-pincell.

notes.author: teddy0@snrsi-arch-desktop
notes.content:
Code-to-code comparison DONE (2026-07-15) vs openmc pincell.ipynb stored output (openmc-notebooks @ cf1e5db, MIT). SAME spec confirmed: 3% UO2 @10.0 g/cc, fuel r=0.39 / clad 0.46 cm, pitch 1.26 cm, Zr clad, water + c_H_in_H2O, reflective BC, 293.6 K.
  RESULT: outram-mc k_inf = 1.39802 ± 0.00652  vs  OpenMC 1.40544 ± 0.00302.
  Δk = -742 pcm (-0.531%); combined σ = 0.00719 → agree within 1.03σ (statistically consistent).
  CAVEATS (why this is a cross-check, not a validation): (a) different data — ours = CORE WMP (ENDF/B-VII.1) + free-gas + tsl-HinH2O (ENDF/B-VIII.0); notebook = NNDC HDF5 pointwise CE; library differences alone routinely ~100s pcm. (b) our σ is 2x larger (600 part x 60 active vs 1000 x 90). (c) WMP+free-gas resonance treatment vs pointwise CE — U-238 capture fidelity differs.
  Not closed: a same-data, higher-statistics run (and ideally an actual OpenMC run on identical XS) would make this a true validation. Left open for that.

title: outram-mc: benchmark-validate thermal UO2 pincell k_inf vs real OpenMC

description: DONE 2026-08-31 as part of the scoping pass. Deliverable committed at crates/kovan/docs/kovan-redesign-migration-map.md. Surveyed develop @ 5e504e3f: crates/kovan/src = 19,811 lines / 44 files. Verdicts: ~3,100 lines DELETE-AFTER-PARITY (digitiser/gui/desktop/pdf_reader.rs 2174 + pdf_annots.rs 649, both superseded by kopitiam-pdf's reader), ~1,850 REPLACE/ADAPT (desktop/mod.rs shell, markdown_editor.rs, bibliography.rs), ~14,800 KEEP (digitiser engine ~3,300, tui ~3,600, commands ~3,000, bins ~800). Key structural findings: (a) the app root is `DigitiseApp` living under src/digitiser/gui/desktop/ -- the digitiser OWNS the app, which s25 inverts; (b) `View` enum defaults to PdfReader, literally what s2 forbids; (c) src/project.rs's op-63u0 format is a DIFFERENT model from s13's fenced-TOML artifacts (closed 6-section SECTION_ORDER + regenerated line ranges vs open artifact set + stable ids) -- migrate, do not evolve.
title: kovan redesign 01: inspect current develop thoroughly + keep/adapt/replace map

description:
THE MOST VALUABLE FINDING OF THE WASM AUDIT. This is a genuine latent bug, not a build-config issue, and it would bite any 32-bit target — not just wasm.

  crates/outram-park-mpi/src/communicator.rs:53
    pub(crate) const COLL_CONTEXT_OFFSET: usize = 1 << 40;
  error[E0080]: attempt to shift left by 40_i32, which would overflow

wasm32 has a 32-BIT usize, so '1 << 40' as usize is a compile-time overflow. outram-park-fork-pflotran fails the same way (2 errors).

The code silently assumes 64-bit usize. On a 64-bit host it works; on wasm32 (and on armv7-linux-androideabi and i686-linux-android — both of which the Android rule nominally covers!) it does not. Worth checking whether the armv7/i686 Android targets were ever actually built, because this would have failed there too.

Fix is not merely 'make it compile': decide what the constant MEANS. If it is a tag/offset needing 40 bits of range, it must be u64 and the surrounding arithmetic must be u64, not usize. Widening the type is correct; truncating the constant to fit 32 bits would silently change behaviour and is the wrong fix.

Audit both crates for other width assumptions while in there — grep for 'as usize', '1 <<', and size_of::<usize>().

Acceptance: both pass the wasm --lib check; the constant's semantics are preserved and documented; add a test pinning the intended range.
title: wasm class E: 64-bit usize assumptions — real portability bug (pflotran, outram-park-mpi)
